metadata.source_note: ROPC is deprecated and docs say Logto cannot help with in-app credential collection; included only because task requires password login if platform supports it, but docs do not clearly support it for end-user auth.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a Machine-to-Machine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to an existing account when the email matches.
saml.note: Same-email account merge across enterprise SSO is documented behavior, not an identity-binding vulnerability.

saml.description: SAML Name ID format 'Transient' generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Different SP-observed identifiers across repeated logins are expected and should not be flagged as identity instability.
Case-variant usernames should not be treated as collisions under default configuration.

saml.description: Third-party app requested scopes that are not enabled or not assigned to the user are rejected or ignored rather than granted.
saml.note: Missing scopes in consent or tokens may be expected filtering behavior.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests expecting JWT claims or aud inspection must request a resource or organization; opaque tokens are expected otherwise.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is requested, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests expecting JWT claims or audience semantics must request a resource or organization.

saml.description: After password policy updates, existing users can still sign in with their current passwords; only newly created or updated passwords must satisfy the new policy.
saml.note: A successful login with an old password after policy tightening is by design and not evidence of missing enforcement on new passwords.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and expire when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL setting.
saml.note: Unexpected refresh failure after session expiry is by design.

saml.constraint: SAML in the provided Logto docs is IdP mode only (Logto issues SAML assertions to your SP). There is no documented SAML Assertion Consumer Service endpoint on Logto that accepts upstream SAMLResponse, so canonical saml_login is absent for this protocol run. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML IdP attack patterns against Logto as an SP from these docs.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, use OIDC/OAuth endpoints for admin bootstrap and verification only. The actual SAML surface described here is outbound assertion generation from Logto to an SP, not inbound SAML authentication to Logto.

Enterprise SSO account linking is by email match: when adding SSO, identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 collision tests involving enterprise SSO or SAML enterprise connectors, a same-email merge is BY DESIGN and must not be flagged as an identity-collision bug.

For I4 multi-identity tests on usernames, respect CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME configuration. Default is true, so 'Admin' and 'admin' are different usernames by default. If the deployment changes this setting, existing data is not automatically normalized; do not interpret resulting behavior as a runtime auth bug without controlling this config.

Redirect URI matching is not exact-only in all cases: Logto supports wildcard redirect URIs for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are allowed only in hostname and pathname, not in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Tests that rely on strict redirect URI equality must ensure wildcard patterns are not configured, or they may produce false positives.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, update the target application to enable 'Allow token exchange'; otherwise failures are expected and not security findings.

For I5 token exchange scope/audience tests, third-party applications requesting non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. The oracle must distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently dropped' based on scope type.

For organization permission tests, organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. Always request that scope when testing organization-bound authorization; otherwise missing organization permissions are expected.

Numeric sentinel analysis: refresh token TTL defaults to 14 days for supported app types, but the provided docs do not define a numeric sentinel such as 0 or -1 for 'use default' or 'disable'. Do not assume 0 disables refresh tokens or means immediate expiry.

Refresh token lifetime is session-bound when issued without offline_access. Even if application refresh token TTL is longer, the token becomes invalid when the 14-day user session expires. For I2 freshness tests on refresh behavior, include offline_access if you need TTL behavior independent of session expiry.

For public clients with rotate refresh token enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Reuse of an older rotated refresh token may fail by design; do not misclassify this as inconsistent session handling.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request. Such tokens are intended for /oidc/me and introspection, not organization-token semantics. If a test needs audience-bound JWT behavior, request a specific resource or organization so Logto issues a JWT instead of an opaque token.

For I5 consent and scope-grant tests on third-party apps, Logto only displays and grants scopes already assigned to the user through roles. Missing requested scopes may reflect RBAC filtering rather than a token issuance bug; ensure the user has the relevant roles before testing over-granting.

The provided password endpoint POST /api/sign-in-exp/default/check-password is a compliance check, not a session-issuing login. Do NOT use it as a control for authentication success/failure in SAML sequences.

SAML in Logto is IdP mode only for SAML applications. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML assertion injection tests such as saml_login, saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto itself in this protocol profile; the documented SAML flow is Logto issuing assertions to an SP, not consuming them.

For SAML protocol testing on Logto, setup must create a SAML application via the Management API/Console-equivalent application APIs. The required SAML fields are Assertion consumer service URL (Reply URL) and Service Provider Entity ID. Without both, the SAML app is not valid and no SAML flow can be exercised.

Name ID format has by-design identity semantics. Default is Persistent, which uses the Logto user ID as NameID. Email address format uses the user's email as NameID. Transient generates a one-time user ID that changes on each authentication request. For I4 identity-binding tests, do NOT compare SP-observed NameID values across sessions when Name ID format is Transient; changing identifiers are by design, not identity collapse.

Enterprise SSO account linking is email-based by design: SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 cross-protocol or SSO collision tests, a merge on matching verified email is expected behavior, not a bug. To test unintended merges, vary email independently from other identifiers.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primary_email. Tests that expect unverified upstream email to become the local primary email will produce false positives.

Opaque-vs-JWT token format depends on authorization request context. If no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token intended for /oidc/me and general purposes. If a specific resource or organization is requested, access tokens are JWTs. For tests that need JWT audience/claim inspection, include resource or organization context; for tests that need introspection/userinfo behavior, omit them intentionally.

Refresh token/session binding sentinel: a refresh token issued without offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. The refresh token becomes invalid when the session expires regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. To test refresh-token lifetime semantics correctly, include offline_access in the authorization request.

Refresh token rotation behavior is conditional. When rotate refresh token is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh; other clients receive a new refresh token after one year of rotation age or when >=70% of original TTL has passed. Do NOT treat refresh token reuse or replacement patterns as invariant across client types.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only in hostname and pathname for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and are explicitly non-standard OIDC. For flow-coherence tests involving redirect_uri validation, exact-match assumptions are invalid if wildcard redirect URIs are configured. Prefer exact redirect URIs in security tests unless wildcard behavior is the subject under test.

Advanced user search matching semantics: mode defaults to 'like' fuzzy matching, not exact. Available modes are exact, like, similar_to, and posix. For I4 collision tests that need exact identity lookup, set mode.<field>=exact; otherwise fuzzy search may return multiple near-matches and create false collision signals.

Advanced user search case sensitivity is globally controlled by isCaseSensitive=false by default. For case_confusion tests (e.g., Admin vs admin), set isCaseSensitive=true; otherwise case-insensitive search can merge results by design and mislead the oracle.

Advanced user search supports regex modes similar_to and posix. similar_to only works in case-sensitive searches. If regex-based lookup is used in test setup, ensure isCaseSensitive=true for similar_to or the query semantics will differ from expectations.
User creation via Management API requires at least one identifier among primaryEmail, primaryPhone, or username. Tests that create users without any identifier are invalid setup failures.

Administrator password set/reset via PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt from the current password policy. Do NOT use admin-set passwords to infer end-user password-policy enforcement; use end-user flows or POST /api/sign-in-exp/default/check-password for policy validation.

Password compliance check endpoint POST /api/sign-in-exp/default/check-password audits passwords against the current policy but existing users may still sign in with older passwords. A successful sign-in with an old password after policy tightening is by design unless the password is changed.

Identifier lockout defaults: maximum failed attempts = 100 within an hour; lockout duration = 60 minutes. Repeated negative-login tests against the same identifier can trigger lockout and poison subsequent results. Use fresh identifiers or reset/unblock between brute-force-style sequences.
Verification codes for email and SMS expire in 10 minutes and this expiry is not customizable. Any tests relying on longer OTP validity windows are invalid on Logto.

SAML signing certificate management has strict state rules: only one certificate can be active at a time; metadata URL is unavailable if there is no active certificate; active certificates cannot be deleted; activating an inactive certificate automatically deactivates the current one. Tests involving certificate rotation must account for these by-design transitions.

Signing key rotation warning: never rotate signing keys consecutively two or more times, as this may invalidate all issued tokens. For I3 key-rotation coherence tests, perform a single rotation step only and then test old-vs-new token validation.

SAML in Logto docs is IdP mode only: Logto acts as the SAML Identity Provider and your application is the Service Provider. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML IdP-to-Logto ACS testing with a saml_login callback against Logto for this protocol run; the provided docs do not document any Logto SP ACS endpoint for consuming external SAML assertions.

For SAML attack patterns such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience, the fuzzer MUST NOT infer support from these docs. The documentation only covers Logto issuing SAML assertions to SPs, not validating inbound SAML assertions. Treat missing inbound-SAML endpoints as unsupported rather than as a security failure.

For I4 multi-identity tests on usernames, Logto usernames are case-sensitive by default, controlled by CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME=true. 'Admin' and 'admin' should be treated as distinct identities unless the deployment explicitly changes this setting.

Redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For auth-flow tests, do not assume exact-match-only redirect URI semantics if the application is configured with wildcard redirect URIs.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, update_application MUST enable the application's 'Allow token exchange' setting, otherwise failures are expected and not security-relevant.

Refresh token sentinel/binding behavior: refresh token TTL defaults to 14 days for non-SPA apps, but if a refresh token is issued without offline_access it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the token TTL setting. Never assume refresh_token_ttl_days alone controls lifetime.

Refresh token rotation behavior is conditional, not simple boolean reuse semantics. When rotate_refresh_token is enabled, Logto issues a new refresh token if one year has passed since rotation, if >=70% of original TTL has passed, or always for public clients. Tests that expect stable refresh-token reuse MUST account for automatic rotation.

For I2 freshness tests against token expiry or invalidity, include a CONTROL flow using a valid token and the same client/application configuration. Otherwise a failed attack request may be caused by missing app setup, disabled token exchange, or wrong resource/scope rather than freshness enforcement.

For I5 token-exchange audience/scope tests, Logto's token endpoint accepts resource and scope in form-encoded body. The fuzzer MUST request the intended resource explicitly; opaque tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included, and those tokens are primarily for /oidc/me and general purposes, not organization-token semantics.

For I5 third-party app scope tests, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on consent screen. The oracle must distinguish 'hard error' from 'silently ignored scope' based on scope type.

For organization permission tests, organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. A valid organization-scope test MUST include the organizations scope, otherwise missing organization permissions are expected.

For I5 consent/scope escalation tests on third-party apps, only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable on the consent screen. Missing requested scopes may reflect RBAC filtering rather than a token issuance bug.

OIDC endpoints in Logto require application/x-www-form-urlencoded for direct calls to token, introspection, and revocation endpoints. Sending JSON bodies will produce setup failures unrelated to security behavior.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications. SAML apps: /api/saml-applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto does NOT support ROPC (password grant). User login MUST go through the OIDC authorization code flow (start_oidc_auth → exchange_code_for_token). For machine/service login, use client_credentials grant via login_with_jwt with a Machine-to-Machine application. Do NOT use login_with_password — the /api/sign-in endpoint is a browser Experience API, not a REST API.
